newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mobutu to see doctors in France again - aide.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu to see doctors in France again - aide.

text.p: Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko, struggling with a rebel war in the country's east, will return to his villa in the south of France on Thursday for consultations with doctors, his spokesman said.

Since coming home three weeks ago, Mobutu effected a major reshuffle in the government and the army high command in preparation for an intended counter-attack on positions held by rebels who have seized a large tract of eastern Zaire.
Mobutu would be leaving from his jungle palace at Gbadolite where he has stayed for much of the time since returning on December 17 from months of cancer treatment and rest in Europe.
"He is leaving tommorrow for health reasons, and in relation to consultations he is due to have with his doctors," spokesman Kabuya Lumuna told Reuters on Wednesday.
Kabuya was unable to say how long Mobutu would remain in France this time.
News pictures of the president broadcast on national television after his meeting with Kenyan leader Daniel arap Moi on Monday showed Mobutu looking tired and drawn.
In France the office of the prefect (government representative) in the French Riviera capital said Mobutu's private flight would land at midday at Nice airport.
The official said Mobutu had an open-ended visa.
Mobutu returned to Kinshasa in December to a huge welcome by well over 100,000 inhabitants of the capital.

But it was a short hour of glory, as Zaire's ruler of 31 years has attracted renewed attack from political enemies since retaining much criticised Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo at the head of a new crisis government formed on Christmas Eve.
